demo.css-position.page_subtitle: Learn the differences between static, relative, absolute, fixed, and sticky through practical examples
demo.css-position.static_b: B (static; top property has no effect)
demo.css-position.relative_description: B moves down 40px, but its original space is preserved → may overlap C
demo.css-position.absolute_description: B is removed from document flow, positioned at parent container's top-left → C moves to B's original position
demo.css-position.absolute_note: 💡 Parent container is set to position: relative, allowing B to position relative to this container
demo.css-position.fixed_description: B is fixed to the bottom-left of the viewport and won't move with page scrolling
demo.css-position.sticky_viewport_descri: The orange bar below uses position: sticky; top: 0, it will stick to the top when you scroll down and it touches the viewport top
demo.css-position.sticky_viewport_bar_ti: 🔖 I am a page-level sticky bar (top:0)
demo.css-position.sticky_viewport_bar_su: I stick to the top of the viewport when scrolling
demo.css-position.sticky_container_descr: The scrollable container below has an internal header using sticky, which only sticks within the container and won't exceed its boundaries
demo.css-position.sticky_container_heade: 📌 I am a container-level sticky header (top:0)
demo.css-position.sticky_container_conte: Content line {number} - This is some demonstration content
demo.css-position.summary_static: Default layout flow, cannot use top/left/right/bottom
demo.css-position.summary_relative: Keeps original space but visually offsets (may overlap other elements)
demo.css-position.summary_absolute: Removed from document flow; positioned relative to nearest non-static ancestor
demo.css-position.summary_fixed: Removed from document flow; positioned relative to viewport, doesn't move with scrolling
demo.css-position.summary_sticky: Flows normally within container, then sticks to boundary when threshold is reached
demo.css-position.summary_note: 💡 Important note: sticky requires threshold values (like top: 0) and only works within the nearest scrollable container. Parent elements with overflow: hidden or transform properties may affect sticky behavior.
